notable_absence.finding: No RBAC role or privilege is named anywhere on this page - not in DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS, or EXAMPLES - despite --create/--delete/--pause/--resume/--settings being cluster-mutating actions. Contrast with bucket- and user-management couchbase-cli pages elsewhere in this tree, which do sometimes cite a role. This is consistent with the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis: the couchbase-cli-xdcr-replicate page only ever says a command 'will fail with an unauthorized error' if the user lacks permission, never naming which role grants it - a lighter-touch, more literal engineering voice than the TW-reviewed RBAC catalogue pages.

cross_component_finding: The --filter-expression flag is documented here in one plain sentence ('A regular expression used to filter the replication stream') with no mention of SQL++ syntax, Number Function exclusions, or the collation/data-type-conversion comparison semantics that the promoted xdcr:filtering-expression concept (built from conceptual/REST pages) carries. This is CLI-vs-REST/UI terminology drift consistent with the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis: the same underlying filtering-expression mechanism is described here as a bare 'regex' with none of the SQL++-subset framing used elsewhere, suggesting the couchbase-cli docs were written by engineers close to the flag's literal type signature rather than by someone cross-referencing the XDCR filtering conceptual model. Separately, --collection-migration and --collection-explicit-mappings are documented as simple mutually-exclusive booleans with no reference to the richer 'migrates by document content, not keyspace' distinction recorded on the manage/ page for the same feature (xdcr:collection-migration) - another instance of the CLI reference being terser than the conceptual doc for the identical mechanism.
